Core Financial System (FFMIA Compliance Initiative)
So here's where we are. We've got this thing hanging over us with FFMIA — basically the
law says our financial management system has to substantially comply with a whole set of
federal requirements, and right now nobody's totally confident we'd pass if someone came
in and checked us against that standard tomorrow. So the real driver here isn't "let's build
something cool," it's "we need a system that can actually stand up when auditors or the
inspector general come knocking and ask us to prove our books are clean and under
control."
The core of it is the general ledger — that's really the heart of everything, every other piece
hangs off of it. We need to be able to classify and track transactions properly: by fund, by
program, by organization, by project, by cost center, all that breakdown, because that's
how budget and program managers actually slice and dice the data later. On top of that we
need solid control over funds so we never end up obligating or spending more than what
was actually appropriated to us, that's a hard line, not negotiable. Then there's the
payment side — vendors, payees, getting money out the door correctly and being able to
track and confirm that a payment actually went where it should. And on the flip side, we
need to handle money coming in too, recording what's owed to the agency and following
up when people don't pay.
Cost management is something we want in there as well, even if it's not glamorous —
being able to actually measure what programs cost and what they're producing matters a
lot for budget conversations down the line. And reporting ties the whole thing together:
management needs timely numbers to make decisions, and we have to be able to produce
the formal financial statements and reports that get sent up the chain, to oversight bodies
and eventually made public.
Who's going to be touching this thing day to day: financial systems analysts, accountants,
program managers, the people who actually run agency operations and need to pull
numbers, and then auditors who'll come in periodically and poke at everything. So usability
for non-technical finance folks matters, this can't be something only an IT person can
operate.
On the technical side we do care about things like making sure it can handle the workload
without falling over, that it talks properly with other systems we already have instead of
becoming an island, that there's a real audit trail and security around who can touch what,
and decent web access so people aren't stuck only using it from one terminal somewhere.
That said, some of the fancier stuff — bells and whistles that are "nice to have" rather than
something a law or regulation forces on us — that's not where we want to spend our first
round of effort. If it's not mandatory and it's not clearly going to make somebody's job
dramatically easier, it can wait, we shouldn't be chasing every optional feature in the first
pass. The priority is getting the mandatory groundwork solid first.

Sistema: Core Financial System

Resumo executivo: The Core Financial System is a federal financial management platform intended to support substantial FFMIA compliance. It provides a controlled general ledger, funds control, payment and receivables management, cost accounting, financial reporting, access control, audit evidence, interoperability, and web access. The system enables agency personnel to maintain accurate books, prevent spending beyond appropriations, support management decisions, and demonstrate financial accountability to auditors and oversight bodies.

Escopo: The system manages and controls the agency's core financial transactions, balances, costs, payments, receivables, reports, and audit evidence.
  Em escopo: General ledger transaction recording and inquiry
  Em escopo: Transaction classification by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center
  Em escopo: Appropriation and funds availability control
  Em escopo: Vendor, payee, and payment management
  Em escopo: Receivables and delinquency follow-up
  Em escopo: Program cost and output measurement
  Em escopo: Management and formal financial reporting
  Em escopo: Audit trails and audit evidence retrieval
  Em escopo: Role-based access control

  Em escopo: Web-based access

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Financial Systems Analyst (Usuário primário): Configure financial structures, monitor interfaces, analyze transactions, resolve processing issues, and support compliance.
  STK-02 - Accountant (Usuário primário): Record, classify, reconcile, and review financial transactions and prepare financial reports.
  STK-03 - Program Manager (Usuário primário): Review program balances, costs, outputs, and management reports for decision-making.
  STK-04 - Agency Operations Personnel (Usuário primário): Retrieve authorized operational and financial information required to run agency activities.
  STK-05 - Agency Management (Usuário secundário): Receive timely consolidated financial information for oversight and resource decisions.
  STK-06 - Auditor or Inspector General (Usuário secundário): Inspect transactions, controls, supporting records, access history, and audit trails.
  STK-07 - Federal Oversight Body (Stakeholder externo): Receive accurate formal financial statements and compliance reports.
  STK-08 - Existing Agency System Owner (Stakeholder externo): Exchange authorized financial data through controlled and documented interfaces.
  STK-09 - Vendor or Payee (Stakeholder externo): Receive correct payments that can be traced to the intended destination.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - FFMIA compliance: Federal financial management activities must substantially comply with applicable FFMIA requirements and related federal standards.
  RN-002 - General ledger authority: The general ledger is the central accounting record for the agency's financial transactions and balances.
  RN-003 - Mandatory accounting classification: Each financial transaction must be classified by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center when those dimensions apply.
  RN-004 - Appropriation limit: An obligation or expenditure must not exceed the amount legally appropriated and available for its funding classification.
  RN-005 - Authorized payment destination: A payment may be issued only to an authorized vendor or payee and must remain traceable to its destination.
  RN-006 - Receivable accountability: Amounts owed to the agency must be recorded, monitored, and subjected to follow-up when unpaid after their due date.
  RN-007 - Program cost measurement: Program costs must be associated with the programs and outputs that consume agency resources.
  RN-008 - Financial reporting: Management and formal financial reports must be based on controlled financial records and approved reporting definitions.
  RN-009 - Financial accountability: Financial actions must be attributable to an authorized individual and retained as evidence for audit.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Post general ledger transaction: The system shall post an authorized financial transaction to the general ledger. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Classify financial transaction: The system shall classify each financial transaction by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Retrieve ledger transactions: The system shall retrieve general ledger transactions using authorized accounting dimensions and date ranges. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Calculate available funds: The system shall calculate available funds for the funding classification of a proposed obligation or expenditure. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Block excess financial commitment: The system shall reject an obligation or expenditure whose amount exceeds available appropriations. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Maintain payee record: The system shall maintain an authorization status for each vendor or payee record. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Initiate payment: The system shall initiate a payment only for an authorized vendor or payee. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Track payment status: The system shall track each payment from initiation through final disposition. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Record payment confirmation: The system shall record confirmation of the destination and disposition of each completed payment. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Record receivable: The system shall record an amount owed to the agency with debtor, amount, origin, and due date. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Calculate receivable balance: The system shall calculate the outstanding balance of each receivable. [Must have]
  RF-012 - Identify delinquent receivable: The system shall identify an unpaid receivable as delinquent after its due date. [Must have]
  RF-013 - Record collection action: The system shall record each follow-up action performed for a delinquent receivable. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Assign program costs: The system shall assign financial costs to an applicable program and output. [Should have]
  RF-015 - Calculate program cost: The system shall calculate program costs for a selected reporting period. [Should have]
  RF-016 - Generate management report: The system shall generate management reports using authorized financial dimensions and periods. [Must have]
  RF-017 - Generate formal financial statement: The system shall generate formal financial statements using approved reporting definitions. [Must have]
  RF-018 - Export approved financial report: The system shall export an approved financial report for submission or public disclosure. [Must have]
  RF-019 - Record audit event: The system shall record an audit event for each creation, modification, approval, rejection, and deletion of financial data. [Must have]
  RF-020 - Administer role permissions: The system shall restrict each financial operation according to the authenticated user's assigned role. [Must have]
  RF-021 - Retrieve audit evidence: The system shall retrieve audit evidence by transaction, user, event type, and date range. [Must have]
  RF-022 - Exchange financial data: The system shall exchange authorized financial data with configured agency systems. [Must have]

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado an authorized accountant and a valid balanced transaction in an open period, quando the accountant submits the transaction, então the system shall assign a unique ledger identifier and set the transaction status to 'Posted'.
  CA-002 - Dado a transaction type requiring all five accounting dimensions, quando the accountant submits the transaction without a cost center, então the system shall reject submission and identify 'Cost center is required'.
  CA-003 - Dado authorized ledger transactions exist for a selected program and period, quando the program manager performs the inquiry, então the system shall return only transactions matching the selected program, authorized scope, and period.
  CA-004 - Dado an appropriation of USD 100000 and recorded commitments totaling USD 60000, quando available funds are requested, então the system shall return USD 40000, subject to the configured currency precision.
  CA-005 - Dado available funds are USD 40000, quando an obligation of USD 40000.01 is submitted, então the system shall reject the obligation, preserve the USD 40000 balance, and display 'Insufficient available appropriation'.
  CA-006 - Dado a vendor record exists, quando an authorized accountant changes its status to 'Authorized', então the system shall save the status, effective timestamp, and responsible user identifier.
  CA-007 - Dado an approved payable references an authorized payee, quando the accountant confirms payment initiation, então the system shall create one payment identifier and set its initial status to 'Initiated'.
  CA-008 - Dado an initiated payment receives a completed status from the payment endpoint, quando the status response is processed, então the system shall set the payment status to 'Completed' and record the response timestamp.
  CA-009 - Dado a payment has completed, quando the completion confirmation is received, então the system shall retain the payee identifier, destination reference, confirmation identifier, amount, and timestamp.
  CA-010 - Dado valid debtor, amount, origin, and due-date data, quando the accountant submits the receivable, então the system shall create one receivable with status 'Open' and an initial balance equal to the submitted amount.
  CA-011 - Dado a USD 1000 receivable has a confirmed payment of USD 250, quando the balance is recalculated, então the system shall return an outstanding balance of USD 750.
  CA-012 - Dado an open receivable has a positive balance and a due date earlier than the current agency business date, quando delinquency evaluation runs, então the system shall set the receivable status to 'Delinquent'.
  CA-013 - Dado a delinquent receivable exists, quando the accountant records a follow-up action, então the system shall append the action type, note, timestamp, and responsible user without overwriting prior actions.
  CA-014 - Dado a valid financial cost and authorized program-output combination, quando the program manager confirms the assignment, então the system shall associate the full assigned amount with the selected program and output.
  CA-015 - Dado a program has USD 80000 in direct costs and USD 20000 in allocated costs for the period, quando the program cost is calculated, então the system shall return a total program cost of USD 100000.
  CA-016 - Dado an authorized manager selects a valid report, period, and program, quando the manager requests generation, então the system shall produce the report with the selected filters and generation timestamp within 3 seconds at the 95th percentile.
  CA-017 - Dado an approved reporting definition and reconciled ledger balances, quando the accountant generates the statement, então the system shall produce a versioned statement whose totals agree with the source ledger within USD 0.01.
  CA-018 - Dado a financial report has approval status 'Approved', quando an authorized user requests export, então the system shall create the configured export file and record its report version, checksum, user, and timestamp.
  CA-019 - Dado an authorized user modifies a financial record, quando the change is committed, então the system shall record the user identifier, timestamp, action, record identifier, and before-and-after values.
  CA-020 - Dado a user lacks permission to approve a financial transaction, quando the user attempts approval, então the system shall deny the operation, preserve the transaction status, and record the denied attempt.
  CA-021 - Dado audit events exist for a specified transaction and date range, quando an authorized auditor performs the search, então the system shall return all matching authorized events ordered by timestamp without exposing events outside the auditor's scope.
  CA-022 - Dado a valid authenticated financial message is received from a configured agency system, quando the message is processed, então the system shall record the financial data once, return a success acknowledgment, and log the interface transaction identifier.

Glossário:
  FFMIA: Federal Financial Management Improvement Act, which establishes requirements for federal financial management systems.
  General ledger: The central accounting record containing the agency's posted financial transactions and balances.
  Appropriation: Legal authority provided to the agency to incur obligations and make expenditures for specified purposes.
  Available funds: The portion of an appropriation remaining legally available after applicable commitments, obligations, expenditures, and other controls.
  Obligation: A legally binding commitment that will result in an immediate or future expenditure.
  Expenditure: The use or disbursement of agency funds to satisfy an obligation or other authorized purpose.
  Fund: An accounting classification identifying a source and legal authority for financial resources.
  Program: An agency activity or group of activities established to achieve defined objectives.
  Cost center: An organizational or operational unit used to accumulate and analyze costs.
  Payee: An authorized person or organization designated to receive a payment.
  Receivable: An amount owed to the agency by an external or internal debtor.
  Delinquent receivable: A receivable with a positive outstanding balance after its applicable due date.
  Audit trail: A chronological, attributable record of actions affecting financial data, configurations, approvals, and interfaces.
  Formal financial statement: A controlled financial report generated according to an approved federal or agency reporting definition.
  RTO: Recovery Time Objective, the maximum target duration for restoring service after a disruption.
  RPO: Recovery Point Objective, the maximum acceptable period of data exposure following a disruption.

Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.
Cadeia de rastreabilidade mínima:
STK → (RN →) RF → HU → CA

A ISO/IEC 25010:2023 define 9 características de qualidade do produto. Todo RNF deve ser 
classificado em uma dessas características. A seguir, cada característica com seus sub-atributos e 
exemplo de RNF.
1. Functional Suitability (Adequação Funcional)
 Functional Completeness — o sistema oferece todas as funções necessárias.
 Functional Correctness — as funções produzem os resultados corretos.
 Functional Appropriateness — as funções facilitam a realização das tarefas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 1. Functional Suitability
O sistema deve calcular o imposto sobre o valor do pedido aplicando corretamente a alíquota de ICMS 
vigente para o estado de destino, conforme tabela oficial CONFAZ, com variação máxima de R$ 0,01 em 
relação ao valor de referência da Receita Estadual.
2. Performance Efficiency (Eficiência de Desempenho)
 Time Behaviour — tempo de resposta e throughput.
 Resource Utilisation — uso de CPU, memória, rede.
 Capacity — limites máximos suportados.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 2. Performance Efficiency
O sistema deve processar no mínimo 200 pedidos por minuto sob carga de 1.000 usuários simultâneos, com 
tempo de resposta inferior a 2 segundos no percentil 95.
3. Compatibility (Compatibilidade)
 Co-existence — coexiste com outros sistemas sem degradação.
 Interoperability — troca dados com outros sistemas.

Core Financial System (FFMIA Compliance Initiative)
So here's where we are. We've got this thing hanging over us with FFMIA — basically the
law says our financial management system has to substantially comply with a whole set of
federal requirements, and right now nobody's totally confident we'd pass if someone came
in and checked us against that standard tomorrow. So the real driver here isn't "let's build
something cool," it's "we need a system that can actually stand up when auditors or the
inspector general come knocking and ask us to prove our books are clean and under
control."
The core of it is the general ledger — that's really the heart of everything, every other piece
hangs off of it. We need to be able to classify and track transactions properly: by fund, by
program, by organization, by project, by cost center, all that breakdown, because that's
how budget and program managers actually slice and dice the data later. On top of that we
need solid control over funds so we never end up obligating or spending more than what
was actually appropriated to us, that's a hard line, not negotiable. Then there's the
payment side — vendors, payees, getting money out the door correctly and being able to
track and confirm that a payment actually went where it should. And on the flip side, we
need to handle money coming in too, recording what's owed to the agency and following
up when people don't pay.
Cost management is something we want in there as well, even if it's not glamorous —
being able to actually measure what programs cost and what they're producing matters a
lot for budget conversations down the line. And reporting ties the whole thing together:
management needs timely numbers to make decisions, and we have to be able to produce
the formal financial statements and reports that get sent up the chain, to oversight bodies
and eventually made public.
Who's going to be touching this thing day to day: financial systems analysts, accountants,
program managers, the people who actually run agency operations and need to pull
numbers, and then auditors who'll come in periodically and poke at everything. So usability
for non-technical finance folks matters, this can't be something only an IT person can
operate.
On the technical side we do care about things like making sure it can handle the workload
without falling over, that it talks properly with other systems we already have instead of
becoming an island, that there's a real audit trail and security around who can touch what,
and decent web access so people aren't stuck only using it from one terminal somewhere.
That said, some of the fancier stuff — bells and whistles that are "nice to have" rather than
something a law or regulation forces on us — that's not where we want to spend our first
round of effort. If it's not mandatory and it's not clearly going to make somebody's job
dramatically easier, it can wait, we shouldn't be chasing every optional feature in the first
pass. The priority is getting the mandatory groundwork solid first.

the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn

Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.
Perhaps your current system is a shapeless mass of history and mystery like the one in Figure 21-2. 
Imagine that you’ve been asked to implement some new functionality in region A in this figure. 
Begin by recording the new requirements in a structured SRS or in a requirements management tool. 
When you add the new functionality, you’ll have to figure out how it interfaces to or fits in with the 
existing system. The bridges in Figure 21-2 between region A and your current system represent these 
interfaces. This analysis provides insight into the white portion of the current system, region B. In 
addition to the requirements for region A, this insight is the new knowledge you need to capture.CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 399

Rarely do you need to document the entire existing system. Focus detailed requirements efforts 
on the changes needed to meet the business objectives. If you’re replacing a system, start by 
documenting the areas prioritized as most important to achieve the business objectives or those that 
pose the highest implementation risk. Any new requirements identified during the gap analysis will 
need to be specified at the same level of precision and using the same techniques as you would for a 
new system.
Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

SRS described just the differences that the new version should exhibit compared to the previous 
version. Nowhere was there a description of the original system. Consequently, everyone had a 
different understanding of the current system’s capabilities. If you’re in this situation, document 
the requirements for your project more thoroughly so that all the stakeholders—both present 
and future—understand what the system does.
Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2 — Características do requisito individual

Pergunta: 'Esta regra existiria sem software?' SIM → RN. NÃO → RF.
Pergunta: 'Menciona tela, botão, banco de dados ou API?' SIM → RF.
Pergunta: 'É uma política de negócio de uma área?' SIM → RN.
É RF ou RNF?
Pergunta: 'Descreve uma AÇÃO do sistema?' SIM → RF.
Pergunta: 'Descreve uma QUALIDADE/PROPRIEDADE do sistema?' SIM → RNF.
Teste: 'O sistema deve [verbo]...' → RF. 'O sistema deve ter [atributo]...' → RNF.
É HU ou RF?
HU = perspectiva do USUÁRIO, linguagem de negócio, descreve NECESSIDADE.
RF = perspectiva do SISTEMA, linguagem técnica, descreve COMPORTAMENTO.
Uma HU geralmente gera 1 ou mais RFs detalhados.

Stakeholder = quem tem interesse no sistema (pode não usá-lo diretamente).
Ator (Caso de Uso) = quem INTERAGE diretamente com o sistema.
Todo Ator é Stakeholder; nem todo Stakeholder é Ator.

Premissa = fato ASSUMIDO como verdadeiro sem confirmação formal. Pode mudar.
Restrição = limite IMPOSTO que não pode ser negociado (lei, orçamento, prazo, tech).

IN = funcionalidade que o SISTEMA DO PROJETO vai implementar.
OUT = funcionalidade que fica em outro sistema ou versão futura.

AÇÃO: varrer o documento inteiro por menções a papéis, departamentos e sistemas externos — 
todos são stakeholders potenciais.

[Necessidade direta] 'eu preciso', 'o vendedor precisa', 'o cliente quer', 'o gestor gostaria'

REGRA DE TRANSFORMAÇÃO: texto bruto → HU no formato Connextra

 2. Identificar O QUE a pessoa quer fazer (ação concreta)

 4. Formatar: 'Como [persona], quero [ação], para [benefício].'

ground_truth:
GABARITO — Project Scenario 9: Core Financial System (FFMIA Compliance Initiative)
Use: "ground_truth" field for RAGAS (context_precision / context_recall).
Each line is an atomic, checkable claim against the scenario text and the
knowledge base — not a full SRS, just the set of facts a well-grounded SRS
for this scenario should be able to cover.

- The system must substantially comply with FFMIA (Federal Financial Management Improvement Act) requirements.
- The general ledger is the central component; every other function depends on it.
- The system must classify and track transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center.
- The system must prevent obligating or spending more than what was actually appropriated (funds control).
- The system must process payments to vendors/payees and confirm that a payment reached the correct destination.
- The system must record and track money owed to the agency (receivables) and follow up when payments are missed.
- The system must support cost management: measuring what programs cost and what they produce.
- The system must produce formal financial statements and reports for management, oversight bodies, and eventual public release.
- Users include financial systems analysts, accountants, program managers, agency operations staff, and periodic auditors.
- The system must be usable by non-technical finance staff, not only by IT staff.
- The system must handle its workload without performance failure and integrate with other existing systems rather than operating in isolation.
- The system must maintain a real audit trail and security controls over who can access what.
- The system must provide adequate web access, rather than restricting users to a single terminal.
- Optional "nice to have" features not mandated by law or regulation are deprioritized in favor of mandatory requirements in the first round.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The general ledger is the central accounting record for the agency's financial transactions and balances.
Each financial transaction must be classified by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center when those dimensions apply.
regras_de_negocio.excecoes: A dimension may be omitted only when formally designated as not applicable to the transaction type.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: An obligation or expenditure must not exceed the amount legally appropriated and available for its funding classification.
regras_de_negocio.fonte: Federal appropriations law and agency funds-control policy

regras_de_negocio.descricao: A payment may be issued only to an authorized vendor or payee and must remain traceable to its destination.
regras_de_negocio.excecoes: Emergency payment procedures formally authorized by agency policy.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: Amounts owed to the agency must be recorded, monitored, and subjected to follow-up when unpaid after their due date.
regras_de_negocio.excecoes: Debts formally waived, written off, or suspended under authorized procedures.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: Program costs must be associated with the programs and outputs that consume agency resources.
regras_de_negocio.excecoes: Shared costs may use an approved allocation method.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: Management and formal financial reports must be based on controlled financial records and approved reporting definitions.
regras_de_negocio.fonte: Federal and agency financial reporting policy
regras_de_negocio.excecoes: Preliminary reports must be explicitly identified as unaudited or provisional.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: Financial actions must be attributable to an authorized individual and retained as evidence for audit.
regras_de_negocio.excecoes: Automated actions are attributed to the service identity and initiating transaction.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system shall post an authorized financial transaction to the general ledger.
The system shall classify each financial transaction by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center.
The system shall retrieve general ledger transactions using authorized accounting dimensions and date ranges.
The system shall calculate available funds for the funding classification of a proposed obligation or expenditure.
The system shall reject an obligation or expenditure whose amount exceeds available appropriations.
The system shall maintain an authorization status for each vendor or payee record.
The system shall initiate a payment only for an authorized vendor or payee.
The system shall track each payment from initiation through final disposition.
The system shall record confirmation of the destination and disposition of each completed payment.
The system shall record an amount owed to the agency with debtor, amount, origin, and due date.
The system shall calculate the outstanding balance of each receivable.
The system shall identify an unpaid receivable as delinquent after its due date.
The system shall record each follow-up action performed for a delinquent receivable.
The system shall assign financial costs to an applicable program and output.
The system shall calculate program costs for a selected reporting period.
The system shall generate management reports using authorized financial dimensions and periods.
The system shall generate formal financial statements using approved reporting definitions.
The system shall export an approved financial report for submission or public disclosure.
The system shall record an audit event for each creation, modification, approval, rejection, and deletion of financial data.
The system shall restrict each financial operation according to the authenticated user's assigned role.
The system shall retrieve audit evidence by transaction, user, event type, and date range.
The system shall exchange authorized financial data with configured agency systems.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The accountant is authenticated, authorized, and the accounting period is open.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The transaction is posted and assigned a unique ledger identifier.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No ledger balance is changed and the rejection is logged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The accountant enters the transaction details.
2. The system validates the required accounting dimensions.
3. The system validates the transaction totals and period.
4. The accountant submits the transaction.
5. The system posts the transaction and records the audit event.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. A dimension is not applicable to the transaction type → the system applies the approved not-applicable designation and continues at step 3.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. A required dimension is missing or invalid → the system rejects submission and identifies the invalid field (ref. RN-003, RF-002).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A proposed obligation or expenditure contains a valid funding classification.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The transaction is accepted only when sufficient funds are available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The transaction remains unposted and available funds remain unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The accountant submits a proposed obligation or expenditure.
2. The system calculates available funds.
3. The system compares the proposed amount with available funds.
4. The system accepts the transaction.
5. The system updates the applicable funds balance.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The proposed amount equals available funds → the system accepts the transaction and sets the remaining available balance to zero.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. The proposed amount exceeds available funds → the system rejects the transaction and displays 'Insufficient available appropriation' (ref. RN-004, RF-005).
2b. Funds validation is unavailable → the system rejects the transaction without changing balances (ref. RN-004, RF-005).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: An approved payable exists and references a vendor or payee record.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The payment is initiated with a traceable status and destination.
fluxo_principal: 1. The accountant selects an approved payable.
2. The system verifies the payee authorization status.
3. The accountant confirms the payment details.
4. The system initiates the payment.
5. The system records the payment identifier and status.
fluxos_alternativos: 5a. The payment processor returns a pending status → the system records the status as 'Pending' for subsequent tracking.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. The payee is unauthorized → the system blocks initiation and displays 'Payee is not authorized' (ref. RN-005, RF-007).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The accountant is authorized to manage receivables.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The receivable is recorded with an outstanding balance and due date.
fluxo_principal: 1. The accountant enters the debtor, origin, amount, and due date.
2. The system validates the required data.
3. The accountant submits the receivable.
4. The system records the receivable.
5. The system calculates its initial outstanding balance.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The receivable has an approved installment schedule → the accountant enters the schedule and returns to step 2.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Required receivable data is invalid → the system rejects submission and identifies each invalid field (ref. RN-006, RF-010).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: An unpaid receivable has passed its due date.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The follow-up action is recorded in the receivable history.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The receivable remains delinquent without a new follow-up record.
fluxo_principal: 1. The accountant retrieves delinquent receivables.
2. The system displays the outstanding balance and prior actions.
3. The accountant selects a receivable.
4. The accountant records the follow-up action.
5. The system timestamps and saves the action.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The receivable has been paid → the system recalculates the balance and removes the delinquent status when the balance is zero.
fluxos_excecao: 4b. The action lacks a required action type or note → the system rejects the entry and identifies the missing data (ref. RN-006, RF-013).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: Costs have been assigned to programs and the user has access to the selected program.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Program costs are calculated for the requested period.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No result is presented as final.
fluxo_principal: 1. The program manager selects a program and reporting period.
2. The system retrieves assigned direct and allocated costs.
3. The system applies approved allocation methods.
4. The system calculates the program cost.
5. The system presents the calculation result.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. No costs exist for the period → the system returns a zero balance identified as having no recorded cost activity.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. An allocation method is missing → the system marks the calculation incomplete and identifies the affected costs (ref. RN-007, RF-015).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The manager is authenticated and authorized for the requested financial scope.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The requested management report is generated from controlled records.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No incomplete report is presented as final.
fluxo_principal: 1. The manager selects a report definition.
2. The manager enters the reporting period and filters.
3. The system validates the user's data scope.
4. The system generates the report.
5. The system displays the report generation timestamp and applied filters.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. The manager selects no optional filter → the system uses the full authorized data scope.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. A requested scope is unauthorized → the system denies the report request and logs the event (ref. RN-009, RF-020).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: An approved statement definition and reporting period exist.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A versioned formal financial statement is generated.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The statement is not marked as complete or approved.
fluxo_principal: 1. The accountant selects the statement and reporting period.
2. The system retrieves controlled ledger balances.
3. The system applies the approved reporting definition.
4. The system validates statement totals.
5. The system generates a versioned statement.
fluxos_alternativos: 5a. The period is not closed → the system labels the statement as 'Provisional'.
fluxos_excecao: 4b. Statement totals fail validation → the system blocks finalization and displays the reconciliation difference (ref. RN-008, RF-017).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The auditor has active read-only audit access.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Matching audit evidence is displayed or exported.
fluxo_principal: 1. The auditor enters transaction, user, event, or date filters.
2. The system validates the auditor's access scope.
3. The system retrieves matching audit events.
4. The system displays actor, timestamp, action, and affected record.
5. The auditor exports the authorized evidence.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. No events match → the system displays 'No audit events found' without altering the filters.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. The requested evidence exceeds the access scope → the system denies access and records the attempt (ref. RN-009, RF-020).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The analyst is authenticated with permission-administration authority.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The role permissions are updated and audited.
fluxo_principal: 1. The analyst selects a role.
2. The system displays its current permissions.
3. The analyst modifies one or more permissions.
4. The system validates the permission combination.
5. The system saves the configuration and records the audit event.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The combination requires additional approval → the system records the change as pending approval.
fluxos_excecao: 4b. The combination violates a configured segregation rule → the system rejects the change and identifies the conflict (ref. RN-009, RF-020).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A configured agency-system interface is active and authenticated.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The authorized data is exchanged and the outcome is logged.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: Unconfirmed data is not treated as successfully exchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. An authorized exchange is triggered.
2. The system validates the interface identity and message.
3. The system processes the financial data.
4. The receiving endpoint confirms processing.
5. The system records the successful exchange.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The endpoint returns a pending response → the system records the exchange as pending and schedules status verification.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Authentication or message validation fails → the system rejects the exchange and records the failure (ref. RN-001, RF-022).

criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall produce the report with the selected filters and generation timestamp within 3 seconds at the 95th percentile.

criterios_de_aceite.dado: an approved reporting definition and reconciled ledger balances
criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall produce a versioned statement whose totals agree with the source ledger within USD 0.01.

criterios_de_aceite.dado: a financial report has approval status 'Approved'
criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall create the configured export file and record its report version, checksum, user, and timestamp.

criterios_de_aceite.dado: an authorized user modifies a financial record
criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall record the user identifier, timestamp, action, record identifier, and before-and-after values.

criterios_de_aceite.dado: a user lacks permission to approve a financial transaction
criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall deny the operation, preserve the transaction status, and record the denied attempt.

criterios_de_aceite.dado: audit events exist for a specified transaction and date range
criterios_de_aceite.quando: an authorized auditor performs the search
criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall return all matching authorized events ordered by timestamp without exposing events outside the auditor's scope.

criterios_de_aceite.dado: a valid authenticated financial message is received from a configured agency system
criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall record the financial data once, return a success acknowledgment, and log the interface transaction identifier.

gabarito_artefatos.observacoes: Jargao regulatorio/contabil abstrato — claims mantidas o mais literais possivel ao texto original para reduzir risco de interpretacao subjetiva. Fornecedores/beneficiarios e pagadores de valores devidos NAO sao stakeholders (nao logam no sistema, sao partes externas afetadas pelas transacoes). Conteudo em ingles porque o cenario-fonte e em ingles (mesma convencao dos gabaritos RAGAS existentes).

em_escopo: General ledger as the central component of the system
Classifying and tracking transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center
Funds control (preventing obligation/spending above the appropriated amount)
Processing payments to vendors/payees, with confirmation of destination
Recording and following up on amounts owed to the agency, including chasing missed payments
Cost management (what each program costs and produces)
Producing formal financial statements and reports for management, oversight bodies, and eventual public release
A real audit trail and security controls over who can access what
Web access, not restricted to a single terminal
Integration with other existing agency systems
fora_de_escopo: Optional ('nice to have') features not required by law or regulation — deprioritized in the first round in favor of mandatory requirements
premissas: PA-01: [INFERRED] The agency already has other existing systems that the financial system needs to integrate with.
PA-02: The system needs to be in substantial compliance with FFMIA before any eventual formal audit.
restricoes: REST-01 (Regulatory): The system must be in substantial compliance with FFMIA (Federal Financial Management Improvement Act) requirements.
REST-02 (Prioritization): Optional features not required by law or regulation are left out of the first round of development.
REST-03 (Usability): The system must be operable by non-technical finance staff, not only by IT staff.

stakeholders.descricao: Financial systems analyst — day-to-day user of the system.
Accountant — day-to-day user, responsible for accounting records.
Program manager — consults cost and performance data of programs for budget decisions.
Agency operations staff — needs to pull numbers from the system to run the agency.
Auditor — periodically reviews the system to verify compliance and control.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The system must never allow obligating or spending more than what was actually appropriated (funds control) — a hard, non-negotiable rule.
The general ledger is the central component of the system; every other function depends on it.
Optional features not required by law or regulation are deprioritized relative to mandatory requirements in the first round.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must maintain a general ledger as its central component, on which the other functions depend.
The system must classify and track transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center.
The system must prevent an obligation or expenditure from exceeding the amount actually appropriated (funds control).
The system must process payments to vendors/payees.
The system must track and confirm that a payment reached the correct destination.
The system must record amounts owed to the agency (receivables).
The system must support following up on/collecting receivables when payment is not made.
The system must support cost management, measuring what each program costs and what it produces.
The system must produce formal financial statements and reports for agency management.
The system must produce formal financial statements and reports for oversight bodies.
The system must support the eventual public release of financial statements and reports.
The system must maintain a real audit trail of who accessed or changed what.
The system must enforce security controls over who can access what.
The system must provide web access to users, instead of restricting them to a single terminal.
The system must integrate with other systems already existing at the agency, instead of operating in isolation.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a financial systems analyst, I want to classify and track transactions by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center, so that program and budget managers can analyze the data.
As an accountant, I want the system to prevent obligations or spending beyond the appropriated amount, so that the agency stays within its funding limits.
As an accounts-payable owner, I want to process payments to vendors/payees and confirm they reached the correct destination, so that disbursements are accurate and traceable.
As an accounts-receivable owner, I want to record amounts owed to the agency and chase overdue payments, so that outstanding amounts are collected.
As a program manager, I want to see cost management data (what a program costs and produces), so that I can support budget decisions.
As agency management, I want formal financial statements and reports, so that I can report to oversight bodies and, eventually, the public.
As an auditor, I want to review a real audit trail and the system's access security controls, so that I can verify compliance during periodic reviews.
As agency operations staff, I want to access the system over the web from multiple locations, so that I'm not restricted to a single terminal.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Record and classify transaction — a user records a financial transaction in the general ledger, classified by fund, program, organization, project, and cost center.
Process vendor payment — the system processes a payment to a vendor/payee and confirms it reached the correct destination, respecting the funds control limit.
Track receivable — the system records an amount owed to the agency and flags it for follow-up when payment is not made.
Generate financial report — a user generates formal financial statements/reports for management, oversight bodies, or public release.
Audit system access — an auditor reviews the system's audit trail and access controls.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a transaction that would exceed the funds appropriated for its fund/program, when it is submitted, then the system prevents the obligation/expenditure from being recorded.
Given a payment issued to a vendor/payee, when the payment is processed, then the system tracks and confirms that it reached the correct destination.
Given a receivable with an overdue payment, when the due date passes without payment, then the system flags the case for follow-up.
Given a request for a formal financial statement, when it is generated, then the result is suitable for submission to management and to oversight bodies.
Given a user accessing the system, when any action is performed, then the system records it in an audit trail that identifies who did what.
